verses.1:1: Now it came to pass in the days when the judges governed that there was a famine in the land; and a man from Bethlehem of Judah went to sojourn in the territory of Moab, he, his wife, and his two sons.
verses.1:2: The name of the man was Elimelech, the name of his wife was Naomi, and the names of his two sons were Mahlon and Chilion—Ephrathites from Bethlehem of Judah. And they entered the territory of Moab and remained there.
verses.1:3: Then Elimelech, Naomi's husband, died, and she was left, she and her two sons.
verses.1:4: And they took for themselves Moabite wives: the name of the one was Orpah, and the name of the second was Ruth. And they dwelt there about ten years.
verses.1:5: Then both Mahlon and Chilion also died, and the woman was left bereft of her two children and of her husband.
verses.1:6: Then she arose, she and her daughters-in-law, and turned back from the territory of Moab, for she had heard in the territory of Moab that the LORD had visited His people, giving them bread.
verses.1:7: So she departed from the place where she had been, and her two daughters-in-law were with her; and they went along the way to return to the land of Judah.
verses.1:8: And Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law, "Go, return each of you to her mother's house. May the LORD deal in lovingkindness with you, even as you have dealt with the dead and with me.
verses.1:9: May the LORD grant you that you may find rest, each in the house of her husband." Then she kissed them, and they lifted up their voices and wept.
verses.1:10: And they said to her, "Surely we will return with you to your people."
verses.1:11: Then Naomi said, "Turn back, my daughters! Why would you go with me? Are there still sons in my womb, that they may become husbands for you?
verses.1:12: Turn back, my daughters, go your way, for I am too old to have a husband. Even if I should say, 'I have hope,' even if I should have a husband tonight and also bear sons,
verses.1:13: would you wait for them until they were grown? Would you restrain yourselves for them from having a husband? No, my daughters, for it is exceedingly bitter for me on your account, because the hand of the LORD has gone out against me."
verses.1:14: Then they lifted up their voices and wept again; and Orpah kissed her mother-in-law, but Ruth clung to her.
verses.1:15: And she said, "Behold, your sister-in-law has returned to her people and to her gods; return after your sister-in-law."
verses.1:16: But Ruth said, "Do not press me to forsake you, to turn away from following you; for wherever you go, I shall go, and wherever you abide, I shall abide. Your people shall be my people, and your God shall be my God.
verses.1:17: Where you die, I shall die, and there I shall be buried. Thus may the LORD do to me, and more also, if anything other than death separates me from you."
verses.1:18: When she saw that she was steadfastly resolved to go with her, she ceased speaking to her.
verses.1:19: So the two of them went on until they came to Bethlehem. And it came to pass, when they came to Bethlehem, that the whole city was stirred because of them; and the women said, "Is this Naomi?"
verses.1:20: And she said to them, "Do not call me Naomi; call me Mara, for the Almighty has dealt very bitterly with me.
verses.1:21: I went out full, yet the LORD has brought me back empty. Why do you call me Naomi, since the LORD has testified against me and the Almighty has brought calamity upon me?"
verses.1:22: Thus Naomi returned, and with her Ruth the Moabitess, her daughter-in-law, who returned from the territory of Moab. And they arrived in Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest.
verses.2:1: Now Naomi had a kinsman on her husband's side, a man of great standing from the clan of Elimelech, whose name was Boaz.
verses.2:2: And Ruth the Moabitess said to Naomi, "Let me go now to the field and glean among the ears of grain after him in whose sight I shall find favor." And she said to her, "Go, my daughter."
verses.2:3: So she departed, and came and gleaned in the field behind the reapers. And as it happened, she came upon the portion of the field belonging to Boaz, who was of the clan of Elimelech.
verses.2:4: And behold, Boaz came from Bethlehem, and he said to the reapers, "The LORD be with you!" And they answered him, "The LORD bless you!"
verses.2:5: Then Boaz said to his servant who was set over the reapers, "To whom does this young woman belong?"
verses.2:6: And the servant who was set over the reapers answered and said, "She is a young Moabite woman who returned with Naomi from the territory of Moab.
verses.2:7: She said, 'Please let me glean and gather among the sheaves behind the reapers.' So she came and has continued from the morning until now, except that she rested a little in the shelter."
verses.2:8: Then Boaz said to Ruth, "Listen, my daughter: do not go to glean in another field, nor depart from this one, but stay close here with my young women.
verses.2:9: Let your eyes be on the field that they reap, and go after them. Have I not commanded the young men not to touch you? And when you are thirsty, go to the vessels and drink from what the young men have drawn."
verses.2:10: Then she fell on her face and bowed down to the ground, and said to him, "Why have I found favor in your eyes, that you should take notice of me, seeing that I am a foreigner?"
verses.2:11: And Boaz answered and said to her, "All that you have done for your mother-in-law since the death of your husband has been fully told to me, and how you left your father and your mother and the land of your birth, and came to a people whom you did not know before.
verses.2:12: May the LORD repay your work, and may a full reward be given you from the LORD, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have come to take refuge."
verses.2:13: Then she said, "May I continue to find favor in your eyes, my lord, for you have comforted me and spoken tenderly to the heart of your maidservant, though I am not like one of your maidservants."
verses.2:14: And at mealtime Boaz said to her, "Come here, eat of the bread, and dip your morsel in the vinegar." So she sat beside the reapers, and he passed roasted grain to her; and she ate and was satisfied, and had some left over.
verses.2:15: When she rose up to glean, Boaz commanded his young men, saying, "Let her glean even among the sheaves, and do not put her to shame.
verses.2:16: Also pull out some for her from the bundles on purpose, and leave it that she may glean, and do not rebuke her."
verses.2:17: So she gleaned in the field until evening, and beat out what she had gleaned; and it was about an ephah of barley.
verses.2:18: Then she took it up and went into the city, and her mother-in-law saw what she had gleaned. She also brought out and gave to her what she had kept back after she had eaten her fill.
verses.2:19: And her mother-in-law said to her, "Where have you gleaned today, and where did you work? Blessed be the one who took notice of you!" So she told her mother-in-law with whom she had worked, and said, "The name of the man with whom I worked today is Boaz."
verses.2:20: Then Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, "Blessed be he of the LORD, who has not forsaken His lovingkindness toward the living and the dead!" And Naomi said to her, "The man is a near relative of ours, one of our kinsman-redeemers."
verses.2:21: And Ruth the Moabitess said, "He also said to me, 'You shall stay close by my young servants until they have finished all my harvest.'"
verses.2:22: And Naomi said to Ruth her daughter-in-law, "It is good, my daughter, that you go out with his young women, and that no one harm you in another field."
verses.2:23: So she stayed close by the young women of Boaz to glean until the end of the barley harvest and the wheat harvest; and she dwelt with her mother-in-law.
verses.3:1: Then Naomi her mother-in-law said to her, "My daughter, should I not seek a place of rest for you, that it may be well with you?
verses.3:2: And now, is not Boaz our kinsman, with whose young women you have been? Behold, he is winnowing barley at the threshing floor tonight.
verses.3:3: Bathe therefore, anoint yourself, put your garments upon you, and go down to the threshing floor; do not let yourself be known to the man until he finishes eating and drinking.
verses.3:4: And it shall come to pass, when he lies down, that you shall mark the place where he lies; then approach, uncover his feet, and lie down, and he himself will declare to you what you are to do."
verses.3:5: Then she said to her, "All that you tell me, I will do."
verses.3:6: Then she went down to the threshing floor and carried out everything her mother-in-law had commanded her.
verses.3:7: And when Boaz had eaten and drunk, and his heart was cheerful, he went to lie down at the end of the heap of grain; and she came softly, uncovered his feet, and lay down.
verses.3:8: Now it came to pass at midnight that the man was startled and turned over, and behold, a woman was lying at his feet.
verses.3:9: And he said, "Who are you?" And she answered, "I am Ruth, your handmaid. Spread the corner of your garment over your handmaid, for you are a kinsman-redeemer."
verses.3:10: Then he said, "Blessed are you of the LORD, my daughter! You have shown even greater lovingkindness at the end than at the beginning, in that you have not gone after the young men, whether poor or rich.
verses.3:11: And now, my daughter, do not fear. All that you say I will do for you, for all the gate of my people knows that you are a virtuous woman.
verses.3:12: Now indeed it is true that I am a kinsman-redeemer; yet there is a kinsman-redeemer nearer than I.
verses.3:13: Remain this night, and it shall be in the morning that if he will redeem you, good—let him redeem you; but if he is not willing to redeem you, then I myself will redeem you, as the LORD lives. Lie down until morning."
verses.3:14: So she lay at his feet until morning, and she arose before one person could recognize another. And he said, "Do not let it be known that the woman came to the threshing floor."
verses.3:15: Also he said, "Bring the shawl that is upon you and hold it out." And she held it, and he measured six measures of barley and laid it upon her; then he went into the city.
verses.3:16: When she came to her mother-in-law, she said, "Who are you, my daughter?" Then she told her all that the man had done for her.
verses.3:17: And she said, "These six measures of barley he gave to me, for he said to me, 'Do not go empty-handed to your mother-in-law.'"
verses.3:18: Then she said, "Wait quietly, my daughter, until you know how the matter will turn out; for the man will not rest until he has settled the matter today."
verses.4:1: Now Boaz went up to the gate and sat down there; and behold, the kinsman-redeemer of whom Boaz had spoken was passing by. So Boaz said, "Turn aside and sit down here, my friend." And he turned aside and sat down.
verses.4:2: Then he took ten men from the elders of the city and said, "Sit down here." So they sat down.
verses.4:3: Then he said to the kinsman-redeemer, "Naomi, who has returned from the country of Moab, is selling the portion of the field that belonged to our brother Elimelech.
verses.4:4: And I thought to inform you, saying, 'Buy it in the presence of those sitting here and in the presence of the elders of my people. If you will redeem it, redeem it; but if you will not redeem it, tell me, so that I may know, for there is no one besides you to redeem it, and I am after you.'" And he said, "I will redeem it."
verses.4:5: Then Boaz said, "On the day you buy the field from the hand of Naomi, you must also acquire Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of the dead, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance."
verses.4:6: Then the kinsman-redeemer said, "I am unable to redeem it for myself, lest I spoil my own inheritance. You yourself redeem my right of redemption, for I cannot redeem it."
verses.4:7: Now this was the custom in former times in Israel concerning redemption and concerning exchange, to confirm any transaction: a man drew off his sandal and gave it to his neighbor, and this was the attestation in Israel.
verses.4:8: So the kinsman-redeemer said to Boaz, "Buy it for yourself." And he drew off his sandal.
verses.4:9: Then Boaz said to the elders and all the people, "You are witnesses this day that I have bought all that belonged to Elimelech, and all that belonged to Chilion and Mahlon, from the hand of Naomi.
verses.4:10: And also Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of Mahlon, I have acquired for myself as a wife, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, so that the name of the dead shall not be cut off from among his brethren and from the gate of his place. You are witnesses this day."
verses.4:11: And all the people who were at the gate, and the elders, said, "We are witnesses. May the LORD make the woman who is coming into your house like Rachel and like Leah, both of whom built the house of Israel; and may you act worthily in Ephrathah and be renowned in Bethlehem.
verses.4:12: And may your house be like the house of Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah, through the offspring that the LORD will give you by this young woman."
verses.4:13: So Boaz took Ruth, and she became his wife; and he went in to her, and the LORD granted her conception, and she bore a son.
verses.4:14: Then the women said to Naomi, "Blessed be the LORD, who has not left you without a kinsman-redeemer this day; and may his name be renowned in Israel!
verses.4:15: And he shall be to you a restorer of life and a sustainer of your old age; for your daughter-in-law, who loves you, has borne him—she who is better to you than seven sons."
verses.4:16: Then Naomi took the child and laid him on her bosom, and she became a nurse to him.
verses.4:17: And the neighbor women gave him a name, saying, "A son has been born to Naomi." And they called his name Obed. He is the father of Jesse, the father of David.
verses.4:18: Now these are the generations of Perez: Perez fathered Hezron;
verses.4:19: and Hezron fathered Ram, and Ram fathered Amminadab;
verses.4:20: and Amminadab fathered Nahshon, and Nahshon fathered Salmon;
verses.4:21: and Salmon fathered Boaz, and Boaz fathered Obed;
verses.4:22: and Obed fathered Jesse, and Jesse fathered David.

notes.1:1: Hebrew literally reads "fields of Moab" here and in verses 2, 6, and 22 (and singular "field of Moab" in verse 6), an idiom for the territory or country of Moab.
notes.1:8: The Qere (read form) is the jussive "May the LORD deal," whereas the Ketiv (written form) displays the full imperfect spelling.
notes.1:13: The Hebrew preposition can be understood either causally ("on your account") or comparatively ("far more bitter for me than for you").
notes.2:1: The Qere (read form) means "kinsman" or "relative," whereas the Ketiv (written form) is a participle meaning "acquaintance."
notes.2:7: Hebrew literally reads "in the house," denoting a temporary shelter in the field for the workers.
notes.2:20: The relative clause "who has not forsaken His lovingkindness" may refer either to the LORD, as translated here, or to Boaz.
notes.3:3: The Qere (read forms) gives plural "your garments" and the standard feminine ending for "go down," whereas the Ketiv (written forms) has singular "your garment" and an archaic feminine ending (similarly for "lie down" in verse 4).
notes.3:9: Hebrew literally reads "Spread your wing," referring to the corner of a garment as a token of marital protection and echoing Boaz's blessing in 2:12.
notes.3:12: The Ketiv (written text) includes a particle that the Qere (read tradition) omits; conversely, in verses 5 and 17, "to me" is supplied in the Qere though not written in the Ketiv.
notes.3:14: The Ketiv preserves a variant spelling of "before," whereas the Qere gives the standard form.
notes.3:15: The Masoretic Hebrew verb is masculine singular ("he went into the city"), referring to Boaz; the Hebrew phrase "six of barley" implies six measures.
notes.3:16: Literally "Who are you, my daughter?"—an idiom asking both for identification in the pre-dawn dimness and how Ruth had fared.
notes.4:1: The phrase "my friend" renders the Hebrew idiom peloni almoni, literally "such-and-such a one," leaving the closer kinsman-redeemer unnamed.
notes.4:4: The Qere reads the cohortative form ("so that I may know"), whereas the Ketiv reads the simple imperfect ("and I will know"); "inform you" translates the literal Hebrew idiom "uncover your ear."
notes.4:5: The Qere reads the second-person verb qanita ("you acquire"), whereas the Ketiv reads the first-person qaniti ("I have acquired"). The Hebrew preposition before Ruth literally means "from," reflecting the legal link between purchasing the estate and marrying the widow.
notes.4:20: The Masoretic Hebrew spells the name Salmah in this verse and Salmon in verse 21.
